single_purpose:
Divinci Local Inference does one thing: it runs an open-weight language model on the user's own GPU, inside their browser, and exposes it as an AI assistant.

The model is loaded once per browser profile into an offscreen document and reached two ways: a side panel the user opens on any page, and Divinci AI's own web app at chat.divinci.app, which can route its chat to the local model instead of a cloud API.

Optionally, the user may sign in to their own Divinci account. That adds page-aware answers grounded in Divinci's public web index, and chat saved to their account. It is off by default and the extension is fully functional without it.

Every permission requested serves that one assistant: hosting the model, storing its settings and history on the device, drawing the panel, and — only when the user signs in — authenticating and fetching page context.
offscreen:
The model runs on WebGPU, and in Manifest V3 a service worker cannot access WebGPU. chrome.offscreen is the supported way to host WebGPU compute in an extension.

The extension creates a single offscreen document that holds the model in memory and runs inference. This is what allows the model to load once per browser profile and be shared by every tab, rather than being re-downloaded and re-initialised per page.

Without this permission the extension cannot run a model at all, which is its only purpose.
storage:
chrome.storage.local holds small key/value data only:

- the selected model id and inference defaults (temperature, max tokens), so the choice survives a service-worker restart
- the user's privacy toggles for the optional signed-in features
- the OAuth token bundle, when the user chooses to sign in, so the token is owned by the background service worker and is never exposed to web pages or content scripts

Model weights are NOT stored here; they are cached separately by the browser's Cache API. Everything in chrome.storage stays on the user's device.
identity:
Used only when the user explicitly clicks "Sign in".

The extension calls chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow to complete a standard OAuth 2.0 authorization-code + PKCE sign-in to the user's own Divinci account. The application is a public client with no client secret.

The resulting access/refresh token is held by the background service worker and is never exposed to web pages or content scripts. Signing out deletes it.

This permission is only needed for the optional signed-in features (page-aware answers and saved chat). A user who never signs in still has full use of the local model.
unlimitedStorage:
Conversation history is kept in chrome.storage.local so that it is shared across every tab and site where the assistant is opened. It cannot live in IndexedDB, because a content script's IndexedDB belongs to the host page's origin, which would silo the user's own history separately per website.

Chatting with a local model is unmetered, so histories grow well past the default quota. Hitting that cap would silently truncate the user's own conversations.

This permission only removes the quota; it stores nothing extra, and none of it leaves the device.
sidePanel:
The assistant can be docked in Chrome's side panel so it stays available while the user browses, rather than closing every time focus leaves a toolbar popup.

chrome.sidePanel is used solely to open and render the extension's own panel when the user asks for it. It reads nothing and is not opened automatically.
host_permission:
Two declared hosts, both used only for the optional signed-in features:

- divinci-prod.us.auth0.com — contacted only during sign-in, for the OAuth token exchange.
- api.divinci.app — receives the authenticated requests: checking whether the current page is in Divinci's public web index, fetching page context for a grounded answer, and saving chat to the user's account.

No other host is contacted for these features.

The content scripts match all sites because the assistant is a general-purpose tool the user opens on whatever page they are reading; which sites those are cannot be known in advance. The content script renders the launcher and panel inside an isolated Shadow DOM. It reads page text only while the panel is open AND the user is signed in, and only to compute a one-way hash locally — the page's content is not transmitted. Banking, webmail, healthcare and authentication pages are skipped entirely.
